blogs.title: Turning Large Language Models into Feature Engineers: The FeatLLM Breakthrough
blogs.description: An overview of the FeatLLM framework that repurposes LLMs from end‑to‑end predictors to automatic rule‑based feature generators for tabular data. The post explains the two‑step prompting strategy, how natural‑language rules are turned into binary features, and why this reduces inference cost compared to prior LLM‑based methods.

blogs.title: Why Feature‑Bagging and Ensembles Make FeatLLM Work on Big Tables
blogs.description: A deep dive into the bagging and ensemble tricks that let FeatLLM handle datasets with hundreds of columns despite prompt length limits. Readers will learn how random feature subsets, temperature sampling, and multiple rule generations improve robustness and mitigate spurious correlations.

blogs.title: From Rules to Predictions: Simple Linear Models Powered by LLM‑Generated Features
blogs.description: Explains the downstream modeling stage of FeatLLM—how binary rule‑features are fed into a lightweight linear model with non‑negative weights, what training looks like in a few‑shot regime, and why this simple model can match or beat heavyweight baselines like XGBoost or TabPFN.

blogs.title: Benchmarks & Real‑World Impact: FeatLLM vs. Traditional and LLM‑Based Tabular Learners
blogs.description: Summarizes the experimental results across 13 diverse datasets, highlighting FeatLLM’s 10% average AUC gain over alternatives such as TabLLM and STUNT. The post also discusses runtime benefits, cost considerations, and potential applications in finance and healthcare where labeled data are scarce.

blogs.title: Designing Prompts for Rule Extraction: Lessons Learned from FeatLLM
blogs.description: Provides a practical guide to crafting the three‑part prompt (basic info, reasoning instruction, response instruction) that coax LLMs into generating high‑quality decision rules. Includes examples, common pitfalls (e.g., noisy syntax), and tips for adapting the approach to other LLM backbones.
